title: Implement Asset Archiving via GraphQL Mutation with Multi-Session Workflow
description: You are a senior C++ developer tasked with adding a critical new feature to the PaletteFlux GraphQL Studio. The request is to implement a 'soft delete' or 'archiving' mechanism for digital assets. This feature must be exposed through a new GraphQL mutation. The implementation must be robust, respecting existing architectural patterns (specifically, the Command Query Responsibility Segregation - CQRS - pattern evident in the codebase) and business rules, such as preventing the archival of assets that are currently in use within a scene. This task will be completed over several sessions, requiring you to retain context and build upon your previous work.

project_spec.name: PaletteFlux GraphQL Studio
project_spec.description:
PaletteFlux GraphQL Studio is a creative-centric API platform that lets digital artists, game designers, and interactive storytellers programmatically compose, remix, and stream multilayer visual assets through a single GraphQL endpoint while exposing complementary REST views for legacy clients. Built on a rigorously applied Model-View-Controller pattern, the project treats each ‘creative asset’ (brush stroke, shader node, animation curve, sound layer) as a first-class model object, controlled by command/query services and rendered to multiple representations (JSON, binary texture atlases, GLSL snippets) depending on the requesting client. 

The application demonstrates how an MVC core can power highly interactive, real-time creative workflows: controllers orchestrate command buses for mutating complex scene graphs, while query handlers gather materialized views optimized for pagination, response caching, and cross-version schema evolution. A unified GraphQL schema allows flexible, client-driven traversal through nested asset relationships, whereas curated REST endpoints serve well-defined, cache-friendly snapshots for CDN distribution. Monitoring hooks, authentication guards, and API-gateway patterns ensure production-grade robustness without sacrificing the free-form expressiveness required by artists and tool developers.
dependencies: cpr or cpp-httplib (outgoing HTTP calls, API gateway)
RapidJSON (high-performance parsing for binary view generation)
